text: Which of the following is a component of the revised Khelo India Scheme for 2021–22 to 2025–26?
options: National Sports Science and Research Programme
National Anti-Doping Testing and Education Network
Creation and Upgradation of Sports Infrastructure
explanation: The revised Khelo India Scheme lists Creation and Upgradation of Sports Infrastructure as one of its five components. The other options are not components named in that scheme structure.

text: Which revised Khelo India component brings together sports competitions, talent identification and community coaching development?
options: Fit India Movement and School Fitness
Khelo India Centres and Sports Academies
explanation: The revised scheme groups sports competitions, talent search and development, and community coaching under Sports Competitions and Talent Development.

text: Which set represents the three national-level Khelo India competitions identified in the revised operational guidelines?
options: Youth Games, National Games and Asian Games
Youth Games, University Games and Winter Games
University Games, National Games and Commonwealth Games
Winter Games, Para-Asian Games and Olympic Games
explanation: The revised operational guidelines identify Khelo India Youth Games, Khelo India University Games and Khelo India Winter Games as annual national-level competitions.

text: A Khelo India talent-identification drive is being planned across several states. Which approach best matches the scheme guidelines?
options: Use transparent performance evidence and scientific testing
Select athletes only from previously famous clubs
Use only coach reputation and informal recommendations
Rank athletes only by their social-media following
explanation: The guidelines describe transparent identification using competitive performance and a scientifically designed battery of tests, with wider access through competitions and talent-search mechanisms.

text: Which revised Khelo India component specifically addresses inclusion through sport?
options: Creation and Upgradation of Sports Infrastructure
Khelo India Centres and Sports Academies
explanation: Promotion of Inclusiveness through Sports is one of the five revised components and covers inclusion-oriented sport initiatives, including participation of groups such as persons with disabilities and women.

text: Which organization is identified in official Indian sports material as implementing the Khelo India Scheme?
options: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
explanation: Khelo India is a Central Sector Scheme of the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports. SAI supports and operates several sports-promotional activities within the national sports ecosystem.

text: The principal purpose of Khelo India national-level competitions is to provide a platform for which of the following?
explanation: The operational guidelines describe Khelo India Games as a platform to showcase sporting skills, spot talent and provide development pathways for gifted athletes.

text: Which event is listed by SAI among the Khelo India national-level competitions and initiatives?
explanation: SAI's current public information lists Khelo India Youth Games, University Games, Winter Games and Para Games among the national-level Khelo India competitions and initiatives.

text: A district has athletes but lacks a safe, usable training venue. Which Khelo India component most directly addresses this gap?
options: Fit India Movement and School Fitness Activities
explanation: A shortage of usable training facilities is an infrastructure gap, so Creation and Upgradation of Sports Infrastructure is the most direct component for the proposed intervention.

text: A state wants to develop continuing local training access around existing facilities and academies. Which Khelo India component is the closest fit?
options: Fit India Movement for School Fitness
Khelo India Centres and Sports Academies
Creation and Upgradation of Sports Infrastructure
explanation: Khelo India Centres and Sports Academies is the component most directly linked with local training structures and academy support, whereas infrastructure creation alone does not describe the continuing training pathway.

subtopic: TOPS and National Sports Development Fund
text: In which year did the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports start the Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS)?
explanation: Official Ministry and SAI material states that MYAS started TOPS in September 2014 to improve India's performance at the Olympics and Paralympics.

subtopic: TOPS and National Sports Development Fund
text: TOPS was revamped to establish a technical support team for managing athletes in which year and month?
explanation: The SAI and MYAS description records that TOPS was revamped in April 2018 to establish a technical support team and provide holistic support to TOPS athletes.

subtopic: TOPS and National Sports Development Fund
text: Which organization currently handles the Target Olympic Podium Scheme according to the official sports-portal description?
explanation: The Ministry's National Sports Development Fund page states that the TOP Scheme is now handled by the Sports Authority of India, with grants provided from NSDF.

subtopic: TOPS and National Sports Development Fund
text: Which body approves customized programmes for athletes selected under TOPS?
explanation: The Mission Olympic Cell is described as approving customized programmes for TOPS athletes and recommending financial disbursement for those programmes.

subtopic: TOPS and National Sports Development Fund
text: A TOPS athlete submits a proposal for overseas training. Which activity falls within the Mission Olympic Cell's stated responsibilities?
options: Issuing the athlete's passport for overseas training
Replacing the athlete's federation in competition
Evaluating proposals and reviewing athlete progress
explanation: The official TOPS description assigns the Mission Olympic Cell responsibility for evaluating proposals and periodically reviewing athletes' progress and performance; it does not replace other institutions.

subtopic: TOPS and National Sports Development Fund
text: What is the principal benchmark described for selecting athletes under TOPS?
options: Popularity in domestic media coverage alone
Number of years in a state academy alone
explanation: Official TOPS information states that selection benchmarks relate to international standards and consistency in performance, with research and consultation also informing identification.

subtopic: TOPS and National Sports Development Fund
text: Which fund provides grants for TOPS-related training, travel and equipment requirements?
explanation: The official NSDF description states that grants from the National Sports Development Fund are placed at SAI's disposal to meet training, travel and equipment requirements of athletes selected in TOPS.

subtopic: TOPS and National Sports Development Fund
text: Which package best represents the type of support that TOPS can provide to a selected elite athlete?
options: Only a domestic participation certificate and medal
Only a rule change and transfer to another sport
Customized training, exposure and equipment support
Only a general physical-education textbook and lecture
explanation: TOPS is intended to provide personalized support, including customized training, foreign or international exposure, equipment and coaching-camp support for selected athletes.

subtopic: TOPS and National Sports Development Fund
text: An athlete has an excellent past reputation but inconsistent recent performances. Which selection approach is most consistent with TOPS criteria?
options: Select automatically because past reputation is sufficient
Reject automatically because only current ranking matters
Review current form, consistency, fitness and benchmarks
Select only after a public vote by national spectators
explanation: TOPS identification considers performance against international standards, current performance, consistency and fitness through research and consultation; past reputation alone is not the stated benchmark.

subtopic: TOPS and National Sports Development Fund
text: What is the best description of the Core and Development groups used within TOPS?
options: Support groups for medal prospects and developing athletes
Two groups separating event officials from spectators
Two groups classifying venues by construction cost
Two groups applying only to anti-doping laboratory work
explanation: TOPS uses Core and Development group pathways to support leading medal prospects and promising athletes at a developmental stage; both are athlete-support categories within the scheme.

text: In which year was the Sports Authority of India established?
explanation: SAI was set up in 1984 as a successor to the legacy of the IX Asian Games held in New Delhi in 1982.

text: Which pair best describes the broad objectives entrusted to SAI?
options: Conducting examinations and licensing private gyms
Running professional sports leagues and ticket sales
Promoting sports and achieving sporting excellence
Regulating international federations and Olympic rules
explanation: SAI's official description gives it the twin objectives of promoting sports and achieving sporting excellence at national and international levels.

text: What is the principal purpose of a SAI National Centre of Excellence (NCOE)?
options: To replace all district sports associations
To provide only short-term recreational activities
To conduct only anti-doping adjudication hearings
To provide specialized training to promising athletes
explanation: SAI describes NCOEs as centres that train promising athletes for excellence in the Olympics and other international events through specialized training and high-performance support.

text: Which combination is specifically described as part of the support available at SAI NCOEs?
options: Only stadium ticketing, advertising and event-broadcasting services
Only academic examinations and non-sport hostel administration
Sports-science backup, individualized diet and staff supervision
Only selection trials without coaching or medical support
explanation: The NCOE description includes state-of-the-art facilities, sports-science backup, individualized diets prescribed by trained nutritionists, and supervision by coaches and qualified support staff.

text: Which abbreviation denotes the SAI Training Centre scheme?
explanation: STC stands for SAI Training Centre. SAI lists STC alongside NCOE, Extension Centres and NSTC among its sports-promotional schemes.

text: Which set of sub-schemes is associated with the National Sports Talent Contest (NSTC) in SAI's scheme description?
options: Olympic cities, World Cups and Asian Games
Regular Schools, IGMA Schools and Akharas
explanation: SAI's scheme description lists NSTC with sub-schemes for Regular Schools and Indigenous Games & Martial Arts (IGMA) Schools and Akharas.

text: An identified athlete needs residential high-performance training, sports-science support and an individualized nutrition plan. Which SAI setting is the closest match?
explanation: NCOEs are designed for specialized high-performance training and provide sports-science backup, individualized diet and overall supervision for promising athletes.

text: Which activity is explicitly included among SAI's key functions?
options: Writing the rules of every sport
explanation: SAI's current official overview identifies talent identification and development as one of its key functions, along with infrastructure, inclusivity, high-performance training and sports-science support.

text: A national training centre asks which SAI function covers specialist clinical care and rehabilitation support for athletes. Which answer is most appropriate?
explanation: SAI's organisational information identifies Sports Medicine and Medical Support as a function providing comprehensive medical care, including specialist services and rehabilitation.

text: What does the abbreviation NSRS represent in SAI's athlete-support ecosystem?
explanation: NSRS stands for National Sports Repository System. SAI's organisational information lists development and maintenance of NSRS among its digital-platform functions.

text: Which body describes itself as the governing body for the Olympic Movement and the Commonwealth Games in India?
options: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
explanation: The Indian Olympic Association states that it is the governing body for the Olympic Movement and the Commonwealth Games in India and administers related governance and athlete-welfare matters.

text: Which responsibility is assigned to the Indian Olympic Association in its official organisational description?
options: Overseeing Indian teams at Olympic, Asian and multi-sport events
Running each National Sports Federation's daily coaching programme
Administering all prohibited-substance laboratory analyses nationwide
Building every SAI training centre without state participation
explanation: The IOA describes overseeing representation of Indian athletes and teams at the Olympic Games, Commonwealth Games, Asian Games and other relevant international multi-sport competitions as part of its role.

text: A Khelo India competition is being organised in a recognised Olympic sport. Which partner should be associated for sport-specific technical coordination under the guidelines?
options: A foreign embassy without a sport body
explanation: The Khelo India operational guidelines state that the concerned National Sports Federations are associated with Khelo India national-level competitions, alongside relevant school, university or winter-sport bodies.

text: Which ministry owns the Khelo India – National Programme for Development of Sports as a Central Sector Scheme?
options: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
explanation: The official scheme description identifies the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports as the ministry implementing the Khelo India – National Programme for Development of Sports.

text: Which authority publishes the official list of recognised National Sports Federations in India?
options: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
explanation: The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports maintains and publishes official recognition information for National Sports Federations, including the ministry's recognised-federation list.

text: For a sport-specific national team, which body normally leads the technical selection and training of competitors, while the IOA handles broader multi-sport representation?
explanation: The IOA's historical and organisational material distinguishes its multi-sport representation role from the sport-specific work of National Sports Federations, which select and train competitors in their sport.

text: The National Sports Development Code of India is primarily associated with governance and compliance of which national sports bodies?
options: Only private fitness clubs and gyms
explanation: Official MYAS materials identify the National Sports Development Code as applying to governance matters involving the IOA and National Sports Federations, including transparency and compliance expectations.

text: The Indian Olympic Association identifies affiliation with which set of international bodies?
options: WADA, NADA, FIFA and ICC sports bodies
UNESCO, WHO, UNICEF and UNDP agencies
IOC, CGF, OCA and ANOC Olympic bodies
FIBA, World Athletics, ITF and UCI bodies
explanation: The IOA organisational page identifies it as affiliated with the International Olympic Committee, Commonwealth Games Federation, Olympic Council of Asia and Association of National Olympic Committees.

text: An Indian delegation is being prepared for a multi-sport event involving several National Sports Federations. Which body coordinates India's broader representation in that event?
options: The federation of only the largest participating sport
Indian Olympic Association for national representation
The event's ticketing and hospitality contractor
A district sports association with no national role
explanation: The IOA states that it oversees the representation of Indian athletes and teams at major international multi-sport competitions, while sport-specific federations retain technical roles.

text: Which arrangement best reflects the coordination model for a Khelo India national competition?
options: A single private sponsor conducts the event without a sport federation
The relevant NSF works with state, school, university and winter bodies
The IOA replaces all local organisers and provides every coach
The anti-doping authority selects athletes and manages schedules
explanation: The Khelo India guidelines describe association with the concerned NSFs and relevant school, university and winter-sport bodies, rather than a single-body or anti-doping-led model.
